identification.summary: DEV-0147 is Microsoft's emerging-threat designation for a China-based cyber espionage actor. On 2023-02-13 Microsoft Security Intelligence said it observed the actor compromising diplomatic entities in South America, which it called a notable expansion of data-exfiltration operations that traditionally targeted government agencies and think tanks in Asia and Europe [S2][S4]. Microsoft said the actor uses ShadowPad (also called PoisonPlug) for persistence and QuasarLoader, a webpack loader, to download and run further malware [S2][S4]. Post-exploitation included abuse of on-premises identity infrastructure for reconnaissance and lateral movement, and Cobalt Strike for command and control and exfiltration [S2][S4].
identification.firstObserved: Public naming: 2023-02-13 (Microsoft Security Intelligence post, per press coverage) [S4]. Earlier activity against Asia and Europe is described only generically [S4].
identification.notes: DEV-0147 is a Microsoft 'development' designation, meaning an unfinalized cluster; no Microsoft final (weather-based) name was found in the sources gathered. The primary post is a short social-media thread; most detail here comes from news coverage of it [S2][S3][S4]. One vendor blog title links DEV-0147 to 'Naplistener' [S7]; NAPLISTENER was not mentioned in the other coverage of Microsoft's post, so this link is unverified.

attribution.confidence: Microsoft describes DEV-0147 as 'China-based' [S4]. No state sponsor, agency or unit is named in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Microsoft's own telemetry-based statement (as relayed by press) [S4]. Press notes ShadowPad is used by several China-linked groups, and Secureworks CTU linked ShadowPad use to MSS-affiliated and PLA-affiliated groups; this is context about the tool, not attribution of DEV-0147 [S2].

objectives: Data exfiltration from government agencies, think tanks and, as newly observed in 2023, diplomatic entities, consistent with espionage [S4].

targeting.notes: South America is the new area as of 2023-02; Asia and Europe are described as the group's traditional focus [S4]. Number, countries and names of South American victims were not published in the sources gathered [S2][S4].

capabilities.summary: ShadowPad RAT for persistent access [S4]; QuasarLoader webpack loader to download and execute additional malware [S2][S4]; Cobalt Strike for C2 and exfiltration [S4]; abuse of on-premises identity infrastructure for recon and lateral movement [S4]. ShadowPad is a modular RAT described as a successor to PlugX, used by multiple China-linked groups, so the tool alone does not identify DEV-0147 [S2][S4]. Microsoft did not disclose the initial-access method; phishing and unpatched applications were commentators' speculation only [S4]. Microsoft said Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint detect the activity and urged enforcement of MFA [S2][S4].

campaigns.name: South American diplomatic entity compromises
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Security Intelligence reported DEV-0147 intrusions at diplomatic entities in South America using ShadowPad, QuasarLoader and Cobalt Strike, with identity-infrastructure abuse for lateral movement. Disclosed 2023-02-13 [S2][S4].

diamond.adversary: China-based espionage actor tracked by Microsoft as DEV-0147; sponsor not named [S4].
diamond.capability: ShadowPad, QuasarLoader, Cobalt Strike, identity-infrastructure abuse [S2][S4].
diamond.victim: Diplomatic entities in South America; historically government agencies and think tanks in Asia and Europe [S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection of diplomatic and policy information, inferred from victim set; Microsoft describes the activity as data exfiltration [S4].
diamond.technology: On-premises identity infrastructure in victim networks was abused; the specific product (for example AD FS) was not named in the sources gathered [S2][S4].

gaps: Primary Microsoft post could not be opened or verified in search results and was removed as a source; details rely on press coverage.
No Microsoft blog or technical report with IOCs, victim count or timeline was found.
Which identity infrastructure was abused (AD FS, Active Directory, Entra Connect) is not stated in the sources gathered.
No state sponsor, MITRE group ID or other-vendor cluster mapping was found; overlap with other ShadowPad users (APT41, REF2924 and others) is unestablished and must not be assumed.
Unverified vendor claim linking DEV-0147 to NAPLISTENER [S7].
No activity after 2023-02 was identified in the searches run; possible later renaming by Microsoft not checked.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Diplomatic networks and their on-premises identity infrastructure are key terrain [S4]. STEP 2: The actor has broadened from Asia/Europe government and think-tank targets to South American diplomatic entities, indicating regional collection interest beyond its earlier footprint [S4]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is persistent RAT (ShadowPad), loader (QuasarLoader), Cobalt Strike C2/exfiltration, and identity-system abuse for lateral movement [S2][S4]; initial access is unknown. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued data exfiltration from diplomatic and government networks using these tools. MDCOA (not sourced; planning hypothesis) is expansion to additional regions' foreign ministries. Candidate indicators: ShadowPad and Cobalt Strike detections, anomalous identity-server queries and authentications, and webpack-loader-style payload downloads [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track Microsoft naming updates for DEV-0147 and ShadowPad reporting; treat the tool as shared across China-linked groups [S2]. Authorities: any partner-network defensive support needs the appropriate legal and policy authority; this record supports none by itself. Mission assurance: harden and monitor on-premises identity servers, enforce MFA, and use endpoint and identity detections Microsoft cited [S2][S4]. Coordination: share indicators with Microsoft, allied diplomatic and CERT partners; verify claims against the primary post .

provenance.importedSummary: DEV-0147 is a China-based cyber espionage actor was observed compromising diplomatic targets in South America, a notable expansion of the group's data exfiltration operations that traditionally targeted gov't agencies and think tanks in Asia and Europe. DEV-0147 is known to use tools like ShadowPad, a remote access trojan associated with other China-based actors, to maintain persistent access, and QuasarLoader, a webpack loader, to deploy additional malware. DEV-0147's attacks in South America included post-exploitation activity involving the abuse of on-premises identity infrastructure for recon and lateral movement, and the use of Cobalt Strike for command and control and data exfiltration.
